name: Project 1143.3 heavy aviation cruiser Novorossiysk (Kiev class)

published.source: ru.wikipedia 'Novorossiysk (aviation cruiser)' after russian-ships.info: 273.1 m overall, flight deck beam 51.3 m, waterline beam 31.0 m, draught 8 m standard / 9.3 m full, keel to masthead 61.6 m

references.name: [D1] Kiev class recognition profile 1986, starboard
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'Kiev class aircraft carrier profile 1986.png' (960 px thumbnail of the 1636 px original)
references.note: A black recognition silhouette on a grey ground. Scaled on the 273.1 m length overall: the hull spans 931 px (columns 12..943), 3.409 px/m; the drawn 274 m bar is 923 px (3.37 px/m), so the drawing's bar and hull disagree by 1.2% and heights read 1.2% higher at the bar scale. Foot (waterline) at row 222; the scale bar below it (rows 226-229) and the caption are outside the window. At 3.4 px/m one pixel is 0.29 m: masts, whips and rails are one or two pixels wide.

references.name: [P1] Novorossiysk 1985 (USN DD-ST-85-06598), from above the starboard bow
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'Kiev-class Novorossiysk DD-ST-85-06598 r.jpg' (US DoD, public domain), 1280 px
references.note: For the reviewer only: forecastle battery order, the one red-orange life-raft rack on the starboard forecastle edge forward of the forward Bazalt pair, the whip aerials on the forecastle edges, the island galleries, paint. Its hull number and markings are not part of the spec.

not_confirmed: the lift sizes (18.5 x 10.3 m drawn for both)
the exact y of the mounts and directors; the directors' identities (drawn as dish posts where D1 shows posts)
the bridge glazing band is drawn on the tower's raked front face at z 32.6
the boats, rudders (not drawn), the anti-fouling colour (dark red-brown drawn)
waterline length: 246.3 drawn from D1's foot against 235.8 published
the masthead whip: D1 shows none above the ball; a 1.2 m whip is a chosen length (the published 61.6 m keel to masthead is not fitted)
the life-raft rack's station (x 78.6..85.4 starboard, six canisters) and the eight forecastle whip stations are read roughly off P1, an oblique photograph (+-4 m)
the forward M-11 director's pedestal (x 30..34.4 from the 22.5 roof): D1 shows the director high there, not how it is carried

D1's island between x -27 and -12 reads 27.3 at -25..-22.7 and 27.0 at -13..-11 against the 23.5 tier drawn; D1's aft island block (14.7-15.0) and the AK-726 (18.5 at -43.8..-39) are drawn at 14.8 and x -42.6; the tiers were not re-cut further
the forecastle reads 0.5-1 m lower on D1 than drawn (14.4 + sheer); not changed: every forecastle mount and the rails stand on it
the forecastle whips' drawn height (about 8.4-9 m): P1 shows them but gives no scale for their length; D1 is too coarse to show them
